soilhub

R client for the Global Soil Data Hub API: discover, read and export harmonised soil profile data (WoSIS, WISE, SOTER, SOTWIS), and, with the appropriate rights, publish derived values. Outputs are ordinary R data frames (or sf objects when you ask for geometries), with the original terms of the sources.

Documentation: https://giulange.github.io/soilhub-r (getting started, articles and the reference of every function).

Install

In the R console (R 4.1 or later), once:

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("giulange/soilhub-r@*release")

R installs the packages soilhub needs by itself. Maps need the optional package sf. Updating, checking and troubleshooting: see the installation page.

First Use 

library(soilhub)
soil <- soil_connect()     # opens the sign-in in your browser (a web address and a code)
soil_datasets(soil)        # the datasets of the hub
x <- soil_observations(soil, datasets = "wosis_points", country = "KEN", max_rows = 100)

x has one row per horizon and one group of columns per soil property. The guide vignette("soilhub", package = "soilhub") explains each step; the other articles cover the raw and revised views, the first layer, exports and publishing.

The old 0.1.x tutorial is kept in docs/legacy/TUTORIAL-0.1.md.

Licences And Citation

The client is MIT licensed. The soil data keep the licences of their providers (ISRIC and the data providers of each profile): before using or publishing results, check them and cite the data with

soil_citations(x)   # what to cite for the data in x
soil_licences(x)    # under which terms

What to cite (the data and the hub) and what the licences allow: see the How to cite page.

Design documents of the package are in docs/design/.
